context.guidance: Send Personal Data and Authentication Secrets in request bodies or headers, never in the path or query string, because URLs are written to logs, caches and browser history. Where an identifier must travel in a URL, use an opaque, short-lived token that reveals nothing about the Data Principal. This keeps the Rule 6(1)(a) protection intact on links that are logged and cached.

value.fix: Stop reading the email from the URL. Replace `const email = query.email` with a value taken from the request body (for example, `const { email } = req.body` on a POST), validated and never placed in the path or query string. If the flow must carry an identifier in a link, send an opaque, random, short-lived token (for example, 128+ bits, single-use or with a short expiry) that the server maps to the Data Principal in its own store, so the URL reveals nothing about the person. Update any client code that builds the link or redirect to use the token or body instead. Also scrub or exclude query strings from access logs, caches and analytics, and add a regression test asserting that `email` is rejected or ignored when supplied in the query string.
